description: SUP-0023 was set up by a buyer with a PO box address and no company registry match. Three invoices were paid before address and bank checks were done.
SUP-0061 had a residential address and a bank account in the name of a buyer's relative. Invoices were paid for goods that were never received.
SUP-0019 was a shell company registered two weeks before its first invoice, using a virtual office address. Paid for services never delivered.
SUP-0047 shared its bank account number with an employee. The vendor had no website, no tax registration and no trading history.
SUP-0036 was a duplicate of an existing supplier with a slightly different name and a new bank account. Not caught because there was no duplicate vendor check.
A spoofed email asked for SUP-0012 bank details to be changed. One clerk approved it without a callback and the next payment run went to the fraudster's account.
SUP-0056 bank details were changed by email request with no independent callback. Two payments were diverted before the real supplier chased.
Same invoice number submitted twice by SUP-0005 for carton supplies. Payment made twice.
SUP-0031 resubmitted an invoice with a trailing space in the invoice number to bypass the duplicate check.
SUP-0067 invoiced the same delivery against two POs. Found when the goods receipt was matched twice.
Eight POs below the 5000 approval limit were raised to SUP-0071 within two weeks, 38000 in total, all approved by one buyer.
SUP-0008 received five POs of 4800 to 4950 on the same day for one requirement. No second approval was triggered.
A buyer and the owner of SUP-0033 inflated prices on five POs. Goods value was about 40% below the amount invoiced.
A warehouse supervisor signed for short deliveries from SUP-0050 in return for payments.
SUP-0008 invoiced quantities above the agreed PO (2500 extra units of fabric) and goods receipt was not checked.
